rows.evidence: Q1: Section II (Materials and Methods) and Section III (Results): the authors collected 60 winter wheat leaves with aphid densities of 0-120 per leaf from an experimental field in Beijing in May 2011, measured leaf reflectance (350-2500 nm) with an ASD spectroradiometer and leaf clip, derived 48 spectral features, and built and validated a PLSR model for aphid density (validation R2 of 0.77, RMSE of 15; Fig. 6).
rows.notes: The study only shows that leaf-level hyperspectral features (including the Aphid Index, GNDVI, RVSI, derivative and wavelet features) correlate with aphid density and that a PLSR model can estimate aphid density on detached leaves in the laboratory. It does not test identification of affected areas within a field (measurements are at single-leaf scale, with aphids removed before measurement), nor any farmer action, pesticide decision or prevention of further damage; the authors explicitly state that upscaling to canopy/field level remains a future challenge. Detection of pest density is a precondition of the claimed pest-control function, so Q2 is no and upstream is set. Minor note: the sensing is proximal leaf-clip spectroscopy rather than airborne/satellite remote sensing, but the technology family (spectral indices for pest detection) is the one named, so no technology mismatch is flagged.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Some numerical values and symbols (coordinates, R2 thresholds, equations) are lost in the text extraction but do not affect the rating.
